title: Is my coffee cold?
until: To cool from {start, number} °{unit} to {cutoff, number} °{unit}.
consent: Use your approximate location to get the outdoor temperature from Open-Meteo?
failed: Outdoor temperature unavailable. You can enter it above.
note: An estimate, not a timer. A lid or insulated mug can change the cooling time.
how: How does the coffee cooling calculator work?
model: Coffee loses heat fastest when it is much hotter than the surrounding air. This calculator uses Newton’s law of cooling with a fixed rate of 0.1 per minute. For coffee starting at 80 °C in a 21 °C room, a 40 °C cutoff gives about 11 minutes, while a 24 °C cutoff gives about 30. If the room is as warm as your cutoff, the coffee won’t cool to it.
privacyDescription: What stays in your browser and what is shared for outdoor weather.
readingsPrivacy: Your browser calculates the cooling time without an account. Edited readings and your unit choice appear after # in the URL. This fragment is not sent to the server, but anyone with the full link can see it. The link never includes coordinates.
weatherPrivacy: Manual entry never requests location. Only after you choose outdoor temperature and confirm does your browser check location permission. It sends latitude and longitude rounded to one decimal place directly to Open-Meteo. The provider receives those approximate coordinates and your IP address. The calculator does not store coordinates.
permissionPrivacy: You can decline and enter the temperature yourself. Change an earlier decision in your browser’s site permissions.
hostPrivacy: Vercel hosts the site and receives ordinary request information such as your IP address and the requested path to deliver the pages.
questionsPrivacy: Questions? Use the public issue tracker without including coordinates or other personal details:
